saml.description: Vault SAML does not validate response or assertion signatures unless the corresponding config flags are explicitly enabled.
saml.source: auth/saml API docs: Create or update configuration
saml.note: A forged or unsigned SAML response being accepted under default config is a hardening issue/insecure default test, not evidence that an explicitly enabled validation check was bypassed.

saml.description: Vault token lookup-self display_name may include the auth mount path as a prefix before the upstream username/alias.
saml.note: Do not flag I4 solely because display_name contains a mount-derived prefix.

saml.description: Multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias name, causing shared privileges, if aliases are administratively reused.
saml.note: This can look like an identity-collision bug but may be caused by explicit alias management rather than SAML login behavior.

saml.description: If default_role is not configured on the SAML auth method, a role must be provided when starting the SAML login flow.
saml.source: auth/saml API docs: config default_role parameter
saml.note: Login failure without a role is expected when no default_role is set.

saml.description: Identity group policies may apply only within the namespace hierarchy unless the global mode is changed to any.
saml.note: Missing cross-namespace group-derived permissions can be by design rather than an authorization-binding failure.

saml.description: SAML group membership is realized through Identity group aliases derived from the configured groups_attribute, not by direct mutation of group member_entity_ids during login.
saml.note: Missing group policies after login may be a setup issue if no matching group alias exists.

saml.description: If the SAML auth method config sets default_role, the login flow may omit an explicit role and Vault will use the configured default role.
saml.source: Vault SAML config docs: default_role is used if no role is provided during login.
saml.note: Do not flag role omission as a binding bypass when default_role is intentionally configured.

saml.description: Enabling verbose_logging causes Vault to log additional potentially sensitive SAML exchange details, including user attributes and full SAML responses at higher log levels.
saml.source: Vault SAML config docs for verbose_logging.
saml.note: Sensitive data in logs under this setting is documented behavior, not necessarily a security flaw in auth logic.

saml.constraint: SAML login is a 3-step flow in Vault: first obtain /v1/auth/{mount}/sso_service_url to get RelayState and token_poll_id, then POST the SAMLResponse to /v1/auth/{mount}/callback, then POST client_verifier and token_poll_id to /v1/auth/{mount}/token. The callback alone does not return the Vault bearer token. Tests for I1/I2/I3 on SAML must preserve this flow coherence and reuse the exact RelayState/token_poll_id/client_verifier tuple generated for that login attempt.

For I1 default-signature-validation tests, Vault SAML configuration defaults are insecure-by-default for signature enforcement: validate_response_signature=false and validate_assertion_signature=false unless explicitly enabled. To test insecure defaults (saml_cert_substitution, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion), leave both unset/false. To test enforcement behavior, explicitly set the relevant flag(s) true; otherwise a successful forged login is by design under the documented default.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, Vault only documents IdP issuer binding via idp_entity_id in /auth/{mount}/config when not using idp_metadata_url. If idp_metadata_url is used, issuer trust comes from metadata; if explicit config is used and idp_entity_id is omitted, setup is invalid. Do not interpret issuer acceptance without a configured trusted issuer source as proof of a bug.

bound_subjects matching semantics are controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, matching is exact string only; if bound_subjects_type=glob, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests, do not set bound_subjects='*' unless bound_subjects_type=glob. With string mode, '*' is literal and only the literal subject '*' matches. To allow multiple distinct subjects through one role, omit bound_subjects entirely or set bound_subjects_type=glob with an intentional pattern.

bound_attributes matching semantics are controlled by bound_attributes_type, which defaults to string. In string mode, attribute values require exact string match; in glob mode, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests, exact-match attribute constraints must be omitted rather than set to wildcard-looking literals. Setting a string-mode bound attribute to '*' matches only the literal '*'.

bound_attributes accepted values are documented as either a single string or a comma-separated list of strings. Vault SAML docs do not specify numeric/boolean cross-type coercion for attribute values. For I5 type-coercion testing, treat bound_attributes as string-oriented and verify whether non-string SAML attribute values are rejected or coerced unexpectedly; do not assume numeric comparison semantics are supported.

token_num_uses on the SAML role limits how many API calls the issued Vault token can make. Every session-authenticated call consumes uses, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the fuzzer performs both a self-lookup and a secret read, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-inspection calls are included. A value of 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses.
Numeric sentinel: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not literal zero. Never use 0 when attempting to test one-time or low-use token behavior.

Numeric sentinel: KV v2 engine config max_versions=0 does not mean keep zero versions; it means use Vault's default retention of 10 versions. Never interpret 0 as immediate deletion of all prior versions.
Numeric sentinel: KV v2 delete_version_after='0s' means versions are not automatically deleted by time-based expiry, not immediate deletion. Do not use 0s expecting instant freshness enforcement.

Numeric sentinel: SAML role token_ttl/token_max_ttl/token_explicit_max_ttl values shown as 0 in read responses indicate default/unset behavior rather than an immediately expired token. Do not treat returned 0 as proof that issued tokens should be unusable.

For I2 replay tests, SAML assertions in Vault must be tested through the full SAML flow and not by replaying only the final Vault token exchange. The security property under test is assertion replay/OneTimeUse handling at the SAML validation stage, so the same assertion ID and/or OneTimeUse condition must be resubmitted through saml_login while preserving the surrounding flow requirements.

For I2 freshness tests against the issued Vault token, include a control login that obtains a valid token and verify it can call lookup-self/read-secret. Otherwise, a failed attack sequence may reflect broken SAML flow setup rather than token freshness enforcement.

For I3 config-change tests, changes to /auth/{mount}/config or /auth/{mount}/role/{role_name} are expected to affect subsequent logins. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of new logins before vs after the change, not expect an already-issued Vault token to be retroactively re-evaluated under new SAML config.

Vault identity group aliases for external groups require the auth mount accessor. The provided SAML docs do not document an endpoint that returns the mount accessor. If group-alias-based I5 tests are attempted, the executor must obtain the accessor out-of-band or skip alias setup; do not invent an undocumented accessor endpoint from these docs.

KV v2 access verification must use the /data/ path segment for reads and writes: /v1/{engine}/data/{path}. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} targets KV v1 semantics and will produce misleading 404/permission results on KV v2 mounts.

KV v2 list operations use /metadata/ paths and require list capability on metadata even if normal reads/writes use /data/. Do not interpret inability to list as inability to read secret data unless the policy under test intentionally omits metadata list permissions.

By documentation, external identity groups are represented through group aliases created from successful login group attributes. For SAML group-policy tests, prefer external groups plus group aliases over manually populating member_entity_ids when modeling upstream group membership, or results may not reflect real SAML group binding behavior.

Global group policy application mode can be within_namespace_hierarchy or any. In enterprise deployments, group-derived policies may or may not apply across namespace boundaries depending on /sys/config/group-policy-application. Cross-namespace I5 tests must account for this setting to avoid false positives when group policies do not propagate by design.

SAML login is a three-step flow in Vault: first POST /v1/auth/{mount}/sso_service_url to obtain RelayState and token_poll_id, then POST the SAMLResponse to /v1/auth/{mount}/callback, then POST /v1/auth/{mount}/token with client_verifier and token_poll_id to obtain the Vault token. A valid I3 test MUST keep these values bound to the same flow instance; mixing RelayState, token_poll_id, or client_verifier across flows will cause by-design failures unrelated to the invariant under test.

For I1 SAML signature-validation tests, do NOT rely on Vault defaults. validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. To test whether Vault verifies the proof it consumes, the fuzzer MUST explicitly set the relevant validation flags in /v1/auth/{mount}/config; otherwise acceptance of attacker-signed or unsigned content may be due to intentionally disabled validation, not a proof-integrity bug.

For SAML default-hardening checks, insecure acceptance with default config is a valid finding surface: if create/update config omits validate_response_signature and validate_assertion_signature, both remain false by default. The fuzzer should distinguish 'accepted under default insecure config' from 'accepted despite validation explicitly enabled'.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, if idp_metadata_url is used, trust and issuer data come from metadata; if static IdP config is used instead, idp_entity_id and idp_cert must both be configured alongside idp_sso_url. Omitting idp_entity_id in static configuration prevents a meaningful issuer-binding test because Vault has no configured IdP entity ID to compare against.

bound_subjects does NOT imply wildcard support by itself. Matching mode is controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, values must match exactly; if bound_subjects_type=glob, '*' is treated as a wildcard. For I4 multi-identity tests, an exact-match bound_subjects constraint MUST be omitted entirely unless all tested identities share the same literal subject.

bound_attributes does NOT imply wildcard support by itself. Matching mode is controlled by bound_attributes_type, which defaults to string. In string mode, attribute values require direct string match; in glob mode, '*' wildcard matching is allowed. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, exact-match bound_attributes constraints MUST be omitted or varied per test identity; setting a string-mode value to '*' matches only the literal asterisk.

bound_attributes accepts expected values as either a single string or a comma-separated list of strings, and authentication succeeds if the SAML attributes match at least one expected value. For I5 tests, this is OR semantics within a single attribute binding, not AND semantics across listed values; the fuzzer must not interpret acceptance of one listed value as overbroad authorization.

groups_attribute controls which SAML attribute values become Identity group alias names. Group-based policy tests must create matching identity group aliases for the exact external group names emitted by that attribute; otherwise missing policies are a setup error, not an authorization-binding failure.

token_num_uses is a session-use budget. Value 0 is a sentinel meaning unlimited uses, not zero uses. Every API call made with the issued token consumes a use, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the fuzzer performs both self-lookup and secret-read verification, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if any additional session-authenticated call occurs before cleanup.

Numeric sentinel: token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 in role reads indicate unset/default-or-disabled semantics rather than a literal zero-second usable token. The fuzzer must not assume 0 means immediate expiry. Likewise token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses. Tests must explicitly set nonzero values when exercising freshness or use-budget behavior.

For I2 replay tests, SAML assertion replay must be tested against the ACS/token flow, not by reusing only the final Vault token. Vault issues a normal Vault token after successful SAML authentication; replay findings must be based on resubmitting the same SAML assertion material (same Assertion ID and/or OneTimeUse condition) through the SAML flow, not on reusing the resulting Vault token.

For I2 freshness tests involving SAML Conditions, include a control login using a valid assertion in the same environment. Without a control, rejection of an expired/future/no-conditions assertion cannot be distinguished from broken SAML flow setup such as bad RelayState, wrong ACS URL, or mismatched client_verifier/token_poll_id.

The acs_url supplied to /v1/auth/{mount}/sso_service_url must be one of the configured acs_urls. If the fuzzer uses an unconfigured ACS URL, callback/token failures are by design and must not be interpreted as security enforcement.

If default_role is not configured on the SAML auth method, a role must be supplied when starting the SAML flow. Tests that omit role without setting default_role will fail by design and cannot be used to assess authorization or identity binding.

External identity groups are intended to receive memberships via aliases from auth methods. For SAML group-mapping tests, use type=external groups plus /v1/identity/group-alias mappings rather than manually populating member_entity_ids to simulate upstream group membership; manual membership changes test Vault identity administration, not SAML group binding.

Entity alias names are security-sensitive identifiers. Vault documentation warns that multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and thereby gain all of its privileges. For I4 collision tests, alias reuse/merge behavior may be administrator-created rather than auth-method-created; the fuzzer must distinguish collisions caused by explicit alias management from collisions caused by SAML login mapping.

Group policy application can be globally configured via /v1/sys/config/group-policy-application. In mode within_namespace_hierarchy (default), group policies only apply within the same namespace hierarchy; in mode any, they apply regardless of namespace hierarchy. Cross-namespace I5 group-policy tests must account for this global mode or they will misclassify by-design namespace scoping as authorization failure or escalation.

KV v2 read paths must use /v1/{engine}/data/{path}, and listing requires /v1/{engine}/metadata/{path}. Using the wrong path shape causes 404/permission mismatches unrelated to SAML-issued token permissions. For verify_read_secret, always use the /data/ path on KV v2 mounts.

SAML login in Vault is a 3-step flow, not a single callback POST. The fuzzer MUST preserve flow coherence by first obtaining flow state from POST /v1/auth/{mount}/sso_service_url, then submitting the SAMLResponse to POST /v1/auth/{mount}/callback with the matching RelayState/InResponseTo, and only then calling POST /v1/auth/{mount}/token with the matching token_poll_id and client_verifier. Reusing callback data across flows or mixing token_poll_id/client_verifier from different flows will cause by-design failures and invalid I3 conclusions.
saml.source: Vault SAML auth API: sso_service_url returns token_poll_id; callback completes round trip; token endpoint requires client_verifier and token_poll_id from the same flow.

saml.constraint: For I1 default-signature-validation tests, Vault's SAML config defaults are insecure-by-default for signature checks: validate_response_signature=false and validate_assertion_signature=false unless explicitly enabled. To test whether insecure defaults accept attacker-signed assertions, configure the SAML auth method with default settings and attempt SAML login. To test enforcement after hardening, the fuzzer MUST explicitly set validate_response_signature=true and/or validate_assertion_signature=true; otherwise a successful login is by configuration, not a proof-integrity bypass.
saml.source: Vault SAML config parameters document both validate_response_signature and validate_assertion_signature default to false.

saml.constraint: For I1 assertion-level integrity tests such as saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_spurious_signature, and saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion, the fuzzer MUST distinguish response-signature validation from assertion-signature validation. Enabling only validate_response_signature checks at least the response signature; enabling only validate_assertion_signature checks at least the assertion signature. To require both layers, set BOTH flags true. Otherwise acceptance of an unsigned assertion may be by design under the configured mode.
saml.source: Vault SAML config docs: each flag independently enables validation for at least response or at least assertion; recommendation is to enable both if IdP signs both.

saml.constraint: For I1 issuer-mismatch tests, when using manual IdP configuration the fuzzer MUST set idp_entity_id in auth config. If idp_metadata_url is used, issuer trust comes from metadata; if manual config is used without idp_entity_id, setup is invalid because the parameter is required when idp_metadata_url is not set. Do not interpret failures from missing manual issuer configuration as secure issuer validation.
saml.source: Vault SAML config docs: idp_entity_id is required if idp_metadata_url is not set.

saml.constraint: For I5 audience/conditions tests such as saml_no_audience_restriction, saml_no_conditions, and saml_wrong_audience, the fuzzer MUST configure entity_id and ACS URLs correctly and compare attack logins against a control login using the same role and valid conditions. The docs only state entity_id must match the SP configuration and ACS URL must be one of configured acs_urls; without a control login, rejection may reflect broken SP setup rather than Conditions/Audience enforcement.
saml.source: Vault SAML config docs require entity_id and acs_urls; callback validates the SAML response.

saml.constraint: bound_subjects does NOT support wildcard matching unless bound_subjects_type is explicitly set to glob. If bound_subjects_type is string or omitted, matching is exact string only and '*' is treated literally. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple NameID values to pass the same role, the fuzzer MUST either omit bound_subjects entirely or set bound_subjects_type=glob with an intentional pattern; do NOT set bound_subjects='*' under default matching.
saml.source: Vault SAML role docs: bound_subjects_type controls string vs glob matching; glob allows wildcard '*'.

saml.constraint: bound_attributes does NOT support wildcard matching unless bound_attributes_type is explicitly set to glob. If bound_attributes_type is omitted, the default is string, requiring direct string matches; wildcard characters are literal. For I4 multi-identity scenarios where different attribute values must all pass, the fuzzer MUST omit the exact-match attribute constraint or intentionally switch to glob mode; do NOT rely on '*' under default string mode.
saml.source: Vault SAML role docs: bound_attributes_type default is string; glob enables wildcard matching.

saml.constraint: bound_attributes values are documented as a single string or a comma-separated list of strings, and authentication succeeds if SAML attributes match at least one expected value. For I5 type-coercion testing, Vault SAML docs do not specify non-string cross-type behavior. The fuzzer SHOULD probe numeric coercion by configuring a numeric-looking bound attribute value and sending alternate lexical forms, but MUST expect that only string semantics are documented. Do not classify outright rejection of non-string claim types as a bug without a successful string control.
saml.source: Vault SAML role docs describe bound_attributes expected values as string or comma-separated list of strings.

saml.constraint: token_num_uses is a session-use budget. Value 0 is a sentinel meaning unlimited uses, not literal zero. Every API call made with the issued session token consumes a use budget, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. Therefore, if the fuzzer performs both a self-lookup and a protected-resource read after login, token_num_uses MUST be at least 2; use at least 3 if an additional session-backed verification call is included.
saml.source: Vault SAML role read response shows token_num_uses; Vault token API documents num_uses=0 means no limit.

saml.constraint: Vault token use limits are enforced across all token-authenticated requests. When testing SAML roles with token_num_uses or any inherited token use limit, the fuzzer MUST account for verification calls consuming uses before the target access test. A 403 on verify_read_secret after a successful verify_granted_identity may be budget exhaustion, not authorization failure.
saml.source: Vault token API: num_uses is maximum uses for the token; lookup-self and secret reads are token-authenticated API calls.

saml.constraint: Numeric sentinel semantics for SAML role token fields follow Vault token behavior: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not zero-use denial. token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 in read responses indicate unset/default-or-disabled semantics rather than a literal immediate expiry. Never assume 0 disables the underlying token or makes it instantly expire; use explicit nonzero values when testing freshness boundaries.
saml.source: Vault SAML role read response shows zero values for token fields; Vault token API documents num_uses=0 as unlimited and TTL fields as configurable durations with defaults.

saml.constraint: For I2 replay tests, a successful first SAML login does not by itself prove replay protection because the docs do not describe assertion-ID or OneTimeUse tracking behavior. The fuzzer MUST run a control valid login and then a second login reusing the same assertion identifier or OneTimeUse-bearing assertion within the same configured trust context. Only acceptance of the second replayed assertion should be treated as evidence of missing replay protection.
saml.source: Vault SAML callback performs validations on the SAML response; replay-specific behavior is not documented in the API.

saml.constraint: For I3 config-change tests, changes to /v1/auth/{mount}/config or /v1/auth/{mount}/role/{role_name} are intended to affect NEW logins. A valid coherence test must compare separate login attempts before and after the admin change, not expect an already-issued Vault token to be retroactively re-evaluated under new SAML config.
saml.source: Vault SAML config and role endpoints configure authentication and resulting Vault tokens; token issuance occurs only at /auth/{mount}/token.

saml.constraint: For I4 group-based identity and I5 group-policy escalation tests, SAML groups are taken from groups_attribute and used as names for Identity group aliases created due to successful login. To make group-to-policy mapping deterministic, the fuzzer MUST create the target identity group and group alias for the SAML mount accessor before login. Otherwise missing alias setup can cause false-negative authorization results unrelated to SAML group handling.
saml.source: Vault SAML role docs: groups_attribute is used as names for Identity group aliases created due to successful login; group-alias API requires mount_accessor and canonical_id.

saml.constraint: Vault identity group type matters for test setup. External groups are intended to represent groups from auth backends via aliases. For SAML external-group mapping tests, the fuzzer SHOULD create groups with type='external' and attach policies there, then map SAML group names through group aliases. Manually populating member_entity_ids is a different mechanism and can confound I5 group-policy tests.
saml.source: Identity group API supports type internal or external; SAML groups_attribute creates identity group aliases from successful login.

saml.constraint: Global group policy application mode can change authorization outcomes across namespaces. If /v1/sys/config/group-policy-application is set to 'any', group policies apply regardless of namespace hierarchy; if 'within_namespace_hierarchy', historical namespace restrictions apply. The fuzzer MUST record or control this setting before concluding I5 group-policy escalation or denial results, especially in enterprise/multi-namespace environments.
saml.source: Vault sys/config/group-policy-application API documents modes within_namespace_hierarchy and any.
